cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said nothing could go wrong and balanced the hall key on my teacup. I taught you to put keys with the invitation, away from drinks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fell in. I used the invitation to dry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered to dry the key, at least. Now the hall address has run into a tea stain. That was our only copy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The key still works. We can scrape the paper off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then scrape it, and ring the bride. Start with good news, as I taught you: 'The key still works.' Then tell her what the tea did to our only copy of the address and ask where to bring it.

reason: Direct spoken edit removes an overclaimed wrapping result, ambiguous food pronoun or explanatory closing flourish. Preserve exact practical consequence and the partner useful contribution.
